analysis:
The supplied units (StandaloneServer.swift base lines 588-1779) contain only unchanged base text. The changed ranges are at base 1964-1971 and 2001-2004 (head 1964-1969 and 1999-2006), outside the visible text. I could see only the truncated patch excerpt for them.

The patch removes the two bracketing computeStandaloneWeightHash passes (pre- and post-load) when glmPlan != nil. It relies instead on the managed GLM load's own SHA-256 verification of every manifest file. The old pre-load check compared the hash against glmPlan.weights.manifest.aggregateSHA256 and threw GLM5NextManagedLoadError.identityMismatch on a mismatch. The new code keeps only glmPlan.weights.recheck() visibly. The post-load comparison is replaced by code that is cut off in the excerpt.

This touches T-012, T-027, T-041 (the cache-eligible weight hash binding) and T-054-style artifact-identity concerns. I could not verify whether the 'verified digest' from the GLM load still feeds preLoadArtifactHash/postLoadArtifactHash. That digest drives cacheEligibleWeightHash and the SSD cache binding, and it must still be compared against the manifest aggregate. A TOCTOU gap between verification and MLX load would matter if a verified digest were ever replaced by an unchecked one. In the visible head, preLoadArtifactHash is `var`, so it is presumably reassigned later. Whether the replacement digest is enforced against glmPlan.weights.manifest.aggregateSHA256 is not visible.

The base-side lifecycle, eviction, reslice and acquire code in the supplied units is unchanged. I found no regression in it, and I treat it only as surrounding context.

Open question for the next pass: confirm that the full head hunk at about lines 1996-2006 still enforces identity equality between the verified GLM digest and the manifest aggregate. Also confirm that recheck() covers the file-change window that the post-load re-hash previously covered.
